subject: Task 11.1 - Canonical provider inventory cache model, boundary, and limits (ADR-018 clauses 1, 5, 6, 7)

findings.summary: The cache's only free-text field (ArrInventoryCacheEntry.LastError) is not redaction-enforced at the cache boundary; it retains an ArrProviderError.Message verbatim.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryCacheEntry holds ArrProviderError LastError. ArrProviderError only trims and truncates its message to 512 characters (no URL/key/control-character redaction), and the cache stores it unchanged. The cache is therefore secret-free only by the caller/producer convention, not by boundary enforcement. Reproduced: a message containing 'GET https://radarr.local:7878/api/v3/movie?apikey=SUPERSECRETVALUE failed' is retained verbatim in the entry.
findings.description: LastError is a bounded free-text carrier with no boundary redaction; secret-freedom depends on the ArrProviderError producer invariant.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs:79,127,245-257 (LastError stored and preserved by WithFailure)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrProviderError.cs:55-64 (Bound trims/truncates only; no redaction)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs:120-135 (TryStore passes caller lastError straight through)

Reproduction (isolated console project under /tmp/final-review/security/repro): LastError.Message retained verbatim: 'GET https://radarr.local:7878/api/v3/movie?apikey=SUPERSECRETVALUE failed'; Contains secret? True
All current producers are fixed code-owned non-secret strings: src/ArrTags/Providers/Sonarr/SonarrClient.cs:232-288,339-363 and src/ArrTags/Providers/Radarr/RadarrClient.cs:207-260,314-338
No caller exists yet (grep: ArrInventoryCache is referenced only by its own file and ArrInventoryCacheTests); the risk becomes live when task 11.2 stores provider failure summaries.

Cross-reference: the same ArrProviderError.Message producer invariant was previously adjudicated LOW/noted in docs/implementation/10.2/security-review.json and docs/implementation/10.3/security-review.json (SEC-10.3-1).
findings.recommended_action: Before wiring the provider client (11.2), enforce redaction at the boundary rather than by convention: route ArrProviderError.Message through a control-character/URL/credential-stripping sanitizer (the existing src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkOperationErrors.Sanitize is the precedent) or sanitize at the cache boundary before storing LastError, and add a regression test that a secret-bearing message is not retained verbatim. Document the non-secret caller contract on ArrInventoryCache.TryStore.

findings.summary: The byte bound is enforced against a conservative estimate that omits several retained fields, so actual retained bytes can exceed InventoryCacheMaxBytes.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryCacheEntry.SizeBytes sums UTF-16 string lengths of a subset of fields plus fixed per-record (256) and per-file (512) overheads. It omits BadgeMetadata.MetadataFingerprint (64 hex chars), ArrRecordIdentity string content, ArrProvider.ProviderInstanceId/DisplayName/ApplicationVersion, AudioFeatures, and object/list overhead, so retained bytes can exceed the configured InventoryCacheMaxBytes by a bounded per-record amount. Memory stays bounded because the record-count bound (<=100000) and the counted variable strings are enforced, so this is an accounting accuracy gap, not unbounded growth; the worker report discloses the estimate as approximate.
findings.description: InventoryCacheMaxBytes is a lower-bound estimate; the record-count bound is the hard memory cap.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs:33-34,306-348 (EstimateSizeBytes enumerates only a subset of fields)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs:130-135 (record-count and byte-bound rejection; no other retained-size enforcement)
src/ArrTags/Metadata/BadgeMetadata.cs:212,238 (MetadataFingerprint is a 64-character hex string, not counted)
docs/implementation/11.1/worker-report.json known_limitations[2] (worker discloses the estimate is not an exact serialized size)
findings.recommended_action: Either include the fingerprint/identity/provider strings in EstimateSizeBytes, or keep the estimate and document explicitly that InventoryCacheMaxBytes is a lower-bound accounting estimate and that InventoryCacheMaxRecords is the hard memory cap. No security action required for 11.1.

findings.summary: The secret-free test guard is name-based and non-recursive and does not cover LastError or nested canonical types, so it is weaker than the 'secret-free cache' claim implies.
findings.issue: InventoryCacheTypesDoNotExposeSecretPropertiesOrFields inspects only the direct property and field names of ArrInventoryCache, ArrInventoryCacheEntry, and ArrInventoryRecordObservation for the substrings Secret/Key/Token/Credential. It does not recurse into nested canonical types, does not include ArrInventoryCacheState, and does not inspect the LastError free-text value. Reproduced: it flags no property on ArrInventoryCacheEntry and would not flag an innocuously-named secret-typed member (e.g. a property named 'Lease' of type SecretLease). It does fail if a top-level secret-named member is added, so it is a real but partial guard; the stronger structural guard is InventoryObservationCarriesOnlyCanonicalProviderNeutralTypes.
findings.description: The secret-free guard is a top-level name heuristic; the structural type guard carries most of the assurance.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrInventoryCacheTests.cs:77-98 (IsSecretName name heuristic) and :266-272 (only Secret/Key/Token/Credential substrings)
tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrInventoryCacheTests.cs:100-117 (stronger structural guard: property types are MatchCandidate/BadgeMetadata, no provider DTO namespace)
Reproduction (isolated console project): Properties flagged by the repo guard: []; Would guard catch a property 'Lease' of type SecretLease? False
The test class omits ArrInventoryCacheState from the type list and never asserts anything about ArrInventoryCacheEntry.LastError.
findings.recommended_action: Strengthen the guard to be structural rather than name-based: assert no member in the cache object graph is assignable to SecretLease, and add an assertion that LastError.Message is bounded and contains no URL/credential shape (or, once SEC-11.1-1 is addressed, that a secret-bearing message is redacted). Until then, phrase the secret-free claim as backed by the canonical-type structural guard, not by the name heuristic.

findings.summary: There is no cache-wide entry-count cap, but the live connection count is fixed at two.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryCache._entries is keyed by ArrConnectionId and TryStore applies no cap on the number of distinct connections retained. ArrConnectionCatalog.FromSnapshot returns exactly two connections (Sonarr and Radarr) and V1 configures at most one per provider kind, so the live bound is two entries. A future multi-connection configuration would need a cache-wide cap.
findings.description: Per-connection bounds only; number of connections is externally bounded to two today.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs:26,137-142 (Dictionary keyed by connection; no entry-count cap)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrConnectionCatalog.cs:21-44 (exactly Sonarr and Radarr)
docs/decisions.md ADR-018 (scope is per ArrConnection; V1 has one connection per provider kind)
findings.recommended_action: No action for 11.1. If a future release allows more than one connection per provider kind, add an explicit cache-wide connection cap.

findings.summary: observedAt is caller-supplied and not clamped to the current time, so a future timestamp would extend the freshness window.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryCacheEntry.ComputeFreshnessWindow derives ExpiresAt/StaleUntil from the caller-supplied observedAt rather than from the store time, and TryStore/TryGet do not reject a future observedAt. A buggy caller passing a far-future observedAt would keep the set 'fresh' beyond the configured TTL from now. observedAt is the local provider read time (not attacker-influenced), and no caller exists yet.
findings.description: TTL is relative to the caller-supplied observation time, not the store time.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs:68,176-194 (freshness derived from observedAt)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs:120-143 (TryStore accepts observedAt without a future check)
findings.recommended_action: No action for 11.1. Optional hardening at 11.2: clamp observedAt to the store time (or reject a future observedAt) so the TTL cannot be extended by a caller defect.

findings.summary: The cache retains raw provider strings as canonical observations; it introduces no path/URL/log sink but consumers must treat them as untrusted.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryRecordObservation retains provider-influenced strings (MatchCandidate.Title/PrimaryPath, provider ids, BadgeMetadata codec/source/custom-badge/extension values). The cache itself performs no filesystem, URL, or log operation on them, so it adds no traversal/injection sink; BadgeMetadata already bounds custom badges (32 x 128 chars) and strips control characters, and MatchCandidate trims and normalizes provider ids. Task 11.2 must keep treating these values as untrusted and must not use PrimaryPath in a filesystem path, provider URL, or log line unescaped.
findings.description: Raw provider strings are stored as observations; the cache is not a path/URL/log sink.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryRecordObservation.cs:16-62 (holds MatchCandidate and BadgeMetadata)
src/ArrTags/Matching/MatchCandidate.cs:86-92,158-174 (provider ids normalized; title/path trimmed)
src/ArrTags/Metadata/BadgeMetadata.cs:294-336 (custom badges bounded and control-character-stripped)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs / ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs (no Path/File/Url/Uri/log usage; grep for Json/Serialize/Log/Console/ToString in the new files returns no matches)
findings.recommended_action: No action for 11.1. Carry this as an explicit input-handling requirement into task 11.2's review.

assessment.secret_free_basis: The cache holds only canonical, provider-neutral types plus non-secret scoping metadata. ArrInventoryCacheEntry stores ArrConnectionId (derived from provider kind and base URL with userinfo and API key excluded), ArrProviderKind, timestamps, a read-only copy of ArrInventoryRecordObservation (MatchCandidate + BadgeMetadata), a bounded ArrProviderError, and SizeBytes. ArrInventoryCacheEntry.From stores only connection.ConnectionId and connection.Provider.Kind, never the ArrConnection, its ApiKeyReference, or any SecretLease. There is no logging, serialization, ToString override, or persistence path in the new files. The one residual is SEC-11.1-1 (LastError free text is not redaction-enforced at the boundary), which is a latent hardening gap rather than a present exposure because no caller exists and all current producers emit fixed code-owned strings.
assessment.bounded_basis: The TTL (1-1440 minutes) and record (1-100000) and byte (1 MiB-256 MiB) bounds are validated at configuration load (OperationalLimits.Validate via AddRangeError) and re-validated at the cache boundary (constructor positivity checks; TryStore rejects an over-record or over-byte entry without storing it). TryGet evicts an expired set; WithFailure preserves ObservedAt/ExpiresAt/StaleUntil and cannot extend the window. The cache is in-memory only, rebuilt empty on restart, and holds at most one entry per connection (two connections today), so retained state is bounded. The byte bound is a conservative estimate (SEC-11.1-2), with the record-count bound as the hard cap; there is no unbounded growth and bound rejection is a safe false return, not a crash.
assessment.non_authoritative_basis: ArrInventoryCache is a standalone in-memory store with no DI registration, no persistence, and no reference to MetadataStateStore or any provenance/artwork-operation store (asserted by InventoryCacheEntryIsDistinctFromThePerItemMetadataStateRecord). It cannot evict authoritative provenance or a non-terminal artwork operation because it is a separate store with no shared state.
assessment.provider_boundary: ArrInventoryRecordObservation carries only MatchCandidate and BadgeMetadata; no Sonarr/Radarr DTO namespace type is reachable from its declared property types. No provider ETag/If-None-Match/revision-token/history-since/SignalR dependency was introduced: the diff does not touch any provider client, and grep for ETag/If-None-Match/IfModifiedSince/SignalR/history in src/ArrTags finds only the pre-existing MediaIdentityFactory ETag usage.
assessment.conclusion: The cache is genuinely secret-free and bounded for its actual data, with no open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM. Three LOW residuals (LastError redaction not boundary-enforced; byte-bound estimate undercounts; name-based secret-free test guard) and three INFORMATIONAL observations are recorded. SEC-11.1-1 and SEC-11.1-3 should be addressed before or during task 11.2, when a provider client first populates the cache.

summary: Task 11.1's provider inventory cache is genuinely secret-free and bounded for its actual data. The cache holds only canonical, provider-neutral types (MatchCandidate/BadgeMetadata) plus non-secret scoping metadata (ArrConnectionId derived without userinfo/API key, ArrProviderKind, timestamps, a bounded ArrProviderError, and a size estimate); it is a standalone in-memory store with no persistence, no logging, no serialization, no ToString exposure, and no reference to authoritative provenance or artwork-operation state, so it is non-authoritative and cannot evict them. The TTL and record/byte bounds are validated at configuration load and enforced at the boundary, over-bound sets are rejected with a safe false return (direct-read fallback), expiry evicts, and WithFailure preserves the bounded last-known-good window. No provider DTO leaks past the provider boundary and no ETag/revision-token/SignalR dependency was introduced. Three LOW residuals are recorded: SEC-11.1-1 (the one free-text field, LastError, is not redaction-enforced at the boundary; reproduced retaining a secret-bearing message verbatim, though no caller exists and all current producers are fixed non-secret strings), SEC-11.1-2 (the byte bound is a conservative estimate that omits the fingerprint/identity/provider strings; the record-count bound is the hard cap), and SEC-11.1-3 (the secret-free test guard is a non-recursive name heuristic that does not cover LastError or nested types). Three INFORMATIONAL observations (no cache-wide connection cap but two connections today; observedAt not clamped; raw provider strings retained with no path/URL/log sink) require no action. There are 0 open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM findings. Verdict: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; SEC-11.1-1 and SEC-11.1-3 should be resolved before or during task 11.2, when a provider client first populates the cache.
